CHAPTER 3 — ORIGINAL TOPIC COVERAGE

Original 3.1 utility functions:
  Corner force balance and sqrt(mu*g*R): chapter_3.md, sections 3.3 and 3.5.
  Straight/curve distance conversion: chapter_3.md, distance helper.
  Accelerator selection: chapter_3.md speed feedback; wheel_control.md explains
  why a target-RPM fraction is not a throttle law for the current engine model.

Original 3.2 basic braking:
  Work-energy derivation, slowing/stopping distance, lookahead over segments,
  early-braking allowance, throttle/brake ordering: chapter_3.md 3.4–3.5.
  Brake pressure, torque capacity and automatic-setup idea: wheel_control.md 5.

Original 3.3 gears:
  Engine/wheel/road-speed relation, up/down thresholds, hunting, indexing,
  torque/slip implications and caching: chapter_3.md 3.6; wheel_control.md 1–2, 8.

Original 3.4 aerodynamic cornering:
  Downforce/drag distinction, cornering derivation, denominator/domain limits,
  lift, wing/body/ride-height coefficients and current mass: braking_math.md 1–2, 8.

Original 3.5 aerodynamic braking approximation:
  Work integral, final-speed rectangle, conservative distance, drag coefficient,
  subdivision/numerical integration, comparison plot: braking_math.md 3–5, 7–8.
  High-speed brake/throttle flicker and model mismatch: chapter_3.md 3.2.
  Simpson/Romberg mentioned as alternatives, without an unearned upper-bound claim.

Original 3.5.S analytical solution:
  Differential equation, initial condition, squared-speed substitution,
  v(s), logarithmic distance, no-aero limit, numerical comparison and physical
  limitations: braking_math.md 6–7 and final section.
  The distance surface over both speeds is retained as a labelled contour map.
  The former unexplained Maple step is now derived explicitly.

Original 3.6 ABS and TCL:
  Wheel-speed ratios, low-speed guards, average-wheel ABS, driven-wheel traction
  control, FWD/RWD/AWD selection, control ordering and limitations:
  wheel_control.md 3–7; implemented in speed.cpp.

Preserved as concepts, modernized as code:
  Local loop variables, nullptr, ordinary header/source separation;
  simple drivetrain selection replaces pointer-to-member plumbing.
  Finite speed caps and checked gear indices replace unbounded/unsafe cases.
  Old lap times/car identifiers and historical hardware remarks are not reused
  as claims about the current simulator. Readers compare their own experiments.

All source and assets are independent of doc/tutorials/robot/.
